texto: In Dutch, the duration of a vowel radically changes the meaning of a word. A double vowel (aa, oo, ee, u) or a single vowel in open syllable represents a long sound, as in «maan» (moon) or «boom» (tree). On the contrary, a simple voice in closed syllable is short, as in «man» (man) or «bom» (bomb). Distinguishing these minimum couples is essential to avoid serious confusion in daily communication.

bloques.pregunta: What is the difference in meaning between «man» and «maan» in Dutch?

opciones.explicacion: The short vocal «a» gives «man» (man), while the long «aa» forms «maan» (moon).
Reverse the concepts and confuse «maan» with «boom».

opciones.explicacion: They are not log variants, but two completely different words.

opciones.texto: There's a tree in the garden.
opciones.explicacion: «In de tuin» places in the garden and «staat een boom» describes a tree standing.

opciones.texto: The man sees the moon in the garden.
opciones.explicacion: It combines the tree («boom») with the moon («maan») and adds a subject that is not there.

opciones.texto: A bomb has fallen in the garden.
opciones.explicacion: It combines the long vowel of «boom» (tree) with the short of «bom» (pump).
